findings.issue: LiveKit API keys read directly from process.env instead of validated env schema
findings.impact: LiveKit credentials (API_KEY, API_SECRET, HOST) bypass Zod validation. A missing or malformed key will fail silently at runtime with empty strings, causing cryptic connection failures.
findings.fix: Add LIVEKIT_API_KEY, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET, LIVEKIT_HOST to the env schema in apps/api/src/config/env.ts with appropriate validation. Import via loadEnv() instead of process.env.

findings.issue: VAPID keys and SMTP credentials read from process.env bypassing environment validation schema
findings.impact: The push notification service reads VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, EMAIL_FROM via process.env directly. Missing values default to undefined without schema-level validation or clear error messaging.
findings.fix: Add VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, VAPID_SUBJECT, EMAIL_FROM to the shared env schema. Import validated values from loadEnv() in all consumers.

findings.issue: API env schema uses .optional() for SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY while worker schema requires them
findings.impact: Drift between environments: API starts without Supabase (degraded mode), worker crashes without Supabase. This inconsistency makes deployment expectations unclear and leads to different behavior per service.
findings.fix: Align API env schema with worker schema: make SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY required. Remove the degraded-mode path or add explicit env flag for running without database.

findings.issue: HEALTH_PORT not defined in any environment schema; read directly from process.env with fallback to 4100
findings.impact: The worker health port is not validated or documented in the shared environment schema. Deployments that set a non-numeric HEALTH_PORT will silently use the fallback.
findings.fix: Add HEALTH_PORT to packages/config/env-schema.ts with number coercion. Default to 4100 in schema, not in code.

findings.issue: No deployment preview environments exist for testing infrastructure changes before production
findings.impact: Infrastructure changes (Docker Compose, Caddyfile, env vars) cannot be validated in an isolated environment before reaching production, risking breaking changes to the live deployment.
findings.fix: Add a staging environment with a separate Docker Compose file and Caddy config. Use Terraform workspaces or separate tfvars files for staging. Wire into CI/CD for auto-deploy on PR.

findings.issue: No .env.example file or env template committed to repository for onboarding
findings.impact: New developers must guess required environment variables by reading code. This slows onboarding and creates risk of missing required config in new environments.
findings.fix: Create .env.example at repo root documenting every environment variable, its type, default, and which service uses it. Add a pre-start check comparing against the schema.

findings.issue: No environment drift detection tooling to compare dev vs staging vs production env configurations
findings.impact: Configuration drift between environments goes undetected until a runtime failure occurs in production that cannot be reproduced locally.
findings.fix: Add a script (scripts/audit/env-drift-check.ts) that compares expected environment variables against actual in each deployment. Integrate into CI/CD as a pre-deploy check.

findings.issue: Console.warn/error used directly in PWA push client instead of structured logging through the application logger
findings.impact: PWA push notification errors in production are not captured in structured logs or Sentry, making debugging push delivery failures difficult.
findings.fix: Replace console.warn/console.error with proper logger calls or Sentry capture. Ensure push notification errors are visible in production observability tooling.

findings.issue: Environment variable documentation does not specify which variables are required per service (api, worker, web)
findings.impact: Operators setting up a new deployment must reverse-engineer which env vars each service needs, increasing setup time and misconfiguration risk.
findings.fix: Annotate each env var in .env.example with a service tag: [api], [worker], [web], [all]. Generate per-service .env.example files from the schema.

findings.issue: Cookie consent stored only in localStorage, which can be programmatically cleared and bypasses server-side consent record
findings.impact: Users who clear localStorage will see the banner again, but the server-side consent record remains stale. Consent state is split between client and server with no synchronization mechanism.
findings.fix: Persist consent state server-side and check it on page load. Add a server-side cookie as the canonical consent source, with localStorage as a cache. Implement a consent revocation endpoint.

findings.issue: Cookie banner offers only binary choice (Accept all / Essential only) with no granular per-category opt-in
findings.impact: Users cannot individually control analytics vs. marketing vs. functional cookies, which may violate GDPR ePrivacy Directive requirements for granular consent.
findings.fix: Implement a tiered consent dialog allowing separate toggles for 'essential', 'analytics', and 'marketing' categories. Store each consent_type independently.

findings.issue: Marketing consent type is accepted and stored but no marketing functionality exists to honor the preference
findings.impact: Consent is collected for 'marketing' purposes without any marketing feature (emails, ads) to respect that preference, creating an audit gap if marketing features are added later without consent re-collection.
findings.fix: Either remove the 'marketing' consent_type until marketing features exist, or add a consent usage audit that maps consent types to actual data processing activities.

findings.issue: No data subject access request (DSAR) workflow for individual user data export or deletion
findings.impact: Users cannot request a copy of their personal data or request deletion under GDPR Article 15/17. The compliance export is admin-only and workspace-scoped.
findings.fix: Implement a user-facing 'Export my data' and 'Delete my account' flow in the settings page. Add a DSAR queue endpoint that collects user data across all tables.

findings.issue: Consent log data retention deletes records but does not anonymize them first for audit chain integrity
findings.impact: Hard-deleting consent logs destroys the audit trail proving consent was given, which may be required by GDPR Article 7(1).
findings.fix: Implement anonymization (nullify IP, user_agent, user_id) before hard-deleting consent logs. Retain a minimal anonymized record permanently.

findings.issue: IP address and user agent stored in plain text in consent_logs without anonymization
findings.impact: PII (IP address, user-agent string) is stored in the database. While useful for security audits, it creates additional GDPR data minimization risk.
findings.fix: Hash or truncate the IP address (e.g., store /24 prefix only). User agent can be stored but should be flagged as PII in data inventory.

findings.issue: No consent revocation UI — once accepted, users cannot change or withdraw consent
findings.impact: GDPR requires that withdrawing consent be as easy as giving it. Users have no way to revoke analytics or cookies consent after initial acceptance.
findings.fix: Add a 'Privacy settings' link in the sidebar or settings page that re-opens the consent dialog. Also clear server-side consent when revoked.

findings.issue: Consent acceptance silently fails on network error; user sees banner dismissed even if server-side record fails
findings.impact: If the POST to /consent fails, the banner disappears but the server has no record of consent. User believes consent was recorded when it was not.
findings.fix: Show an error state or retry mechanism if consent persistence fails. Only dismiss the banner after server confirms the consent record.

findings.issue: Production deployment workflow lacks mandatory manual approval step before deployment to production
findings.impact: Any push to main or manual trigger deploys to production without human oversight. A malicious or buggy commit reaches users with no opportunity for review or rollback decision.
findings.fix: Add an 'environment: production' deployment protection rule with required reviewers in GitHub. Add a 'wait-for-approval' step before the deploy job that blocks until an authorized user approves.

findings.issue: CI/CD uses `:latest` image tags which overwrite previous production images, preventing rapid rollback to a known-good version
findings.impact: If a broken deployment is promoted to production, rolling back requires rebuilding the old image instead of redeploying a tagged version. The previous `:latest` image is lost.
findings.fix: Tag production images with both `:latest` and a specific SHA-based tag (e.g., `:git-sha-${GITHUB_SHA}`). Add a rollback workflow that accepts a SHA tag and deploys that version.

findings.issue: Production Docker Compose uses Caddy for TLS while development uses raw ports — no parity on reverse proxy configuration
findings.impact: CORS, cookie security settings, and CSP headers behave differently between environments. A bug in Caddy config only manifests in production, and production TLS issues cannot be reproduced locally.
findings.fix: Add a local Caddyfile.dev for development that mirrors production Caddy configuration but with self-signed certs. Add a docker-compose.override.yml for local TLS testing.

findings.issue: Development deployment to DigitalOcean uses same Docker Compose as production with only minor env var differences
findings.impact: A breaking change in Docker Compose that only manifests on the remote environment cannot be detected before promoting to production. Dev and prod should run independently as isolated stacks.
findings.fix: Use separate Docker Compose project names (--project-name) to isolate stacks. Add environment prefix to container names. Ensure dev and prod can coexist on the same host without conflict.

findings.issue: No smoke test or health check validation step after production deployment completes
findings.impact: A deployment that starts but immediately fails health checks goes undetected by CI/CD. Operators only learn about failures through user reports.
findings.fix: Add a post-deploy smoke test step that: (1) hits the /health endpoint, (2) verifies 200 response, (3) checks database connectivity, (4) sends a test WebSocket message. Rollback automatically if smoke tests fail.

findings.issue: Terraform IaC only provisions a single droplet shared between dev and prod environments
findings.impact: Development and production share the same compute resources. A load test or memory leak in dev can impact production performance and vice versa.
findings.fix: Separate Terraform workspaces for dev and prod with isolated droplets. Add environment variable to Terraform to select target. Increase resource allocation for prod.
